content:
Ahead of Apple's special event, Bloomberg publishes a new report detailing the decade-long development journey of Apple's foldable iPhone.

The report notably mentions former Apple CEO Tim Cook's involvement in the project and reveals the possible price of the foldable iPhone.

Mark Gurman says Apple engineers began development on the iPhone Fold around 2016. In 2020, after Tim Cook returned from a China trip, he was "extraordinarily excited" about foldable phones. He reportedly pushed Apple's hardware team to accelerate development of the company's first foldable product.

Generally speaking, Tim Cook "does not get involved in conceiving new products." So his personal involvement in the foldable iPhone's development adds considerable weight to the project.

Regarding the pricing of the foldable iPhone (which Apple internally refers to as the iPhone Ultra), the company's original goal was a starting price of US$1,999. However, due to recent increases in component costs, the target has been adjusted to US$2,199.

According to one person familiar with the matter, Apple recently discussed pricing the foldable product at US$2,199, and noted that multiple options were considered in recent weeks, adding that memory supply tightness has pushed up the company's cost budget. Some higher-capacity versions of the product could be priced near US$3,000. By comparison, the standard iPhone currently starts at US$799, while the iPhone 17 Pro starts at US$1,099.

Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone Ultra tomorrow for the first time. 9to5Mac will be live at the Steve Jobs Theater to bring you in-depth coverage of everything.
